- The mechanism, read by the seat in the diff: the run writes `$GIT_DIR/os-regen-merge-base` (version · phase · base · branch_tip · main_tip · branch · written · `conflicted=` rows) as `pending` BEFORE step 1 and marks it `done` after step 2. `rr_classify`: an unreadable record or a recorded branch tip that is not an ancestor of HEAD ⇒ `stale`, refused with the record printed; the recorded main tip contained in HEAD ⇒ `rerun` while pending, `settled` when done and `origin/main` has not moved (reported, exit 0), `plain` when it has (a new merge, a new record); no record and `origin/main` already in HEAD ⇒ `orphan`, refused non-zero with the by-hand step 2 computed from the merge commit's own two parents; otherwise `plain`. The rerun skips step 1 and runs step 2 against the RECORDED base with `main_side` pinned to the recorded main tip — also on the plain path — and keeps the operator's resolution of the recorded conflicted paths instead of taking main's side of them. All four conflict exits emit one instruction from `rr_rerun_instruction`. ⛔ Nothing guesses a base; `--base` stays absent; the `os-regen-pending` marker is neither written nor read (the three sibling scripts untouched).
- Two of the dispatch's hypotheses corrected by measurement, both correctly: containment is asked against the RECORDED main tip, not `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` == `origin/main` (a shared ref a sibling's fetch advances between the conflict and the rerun); the record is marked done rather than deleted, because a completed run and an unperformed rerun leave identical trees and deletion would make the loud refusal fire on a finished merge — idempotence is met by the `settled` reading instead. The card's count corrected too: four conflict exits, and the fourth (class 2 only) said 「continue with step 4」, omitting step 2 outright — repaired here under the bounded in-place rule (same file, same defect class, no new verification surface), which the seat accepts.
- Behaviour change the seat names: a branch that already contains `origin/main` with no record now exits 1 (`orphan`) where the old code ran a no-op merge, an inert step 2 and step 4 with exit 0. Accepted: that tree is indistinguishable from the dead end the card names, the refusal says so and states the outcome (「this refusal IS the whole outcome」 when nothing was merged), and regeneration alone has its own tool. A safety direction on a PM instrument — the seat's call, not a maintainer question.
